mainTopic: How we know an אונן's עבודה is invalid (via הצד השוה and רב משרשיא's קל וחומר), and רבא's limit of the rule to a קרבן יחיד, challenged by רבא בר אהילאי
overview: The גמרא wants to prove that an אונן who does the עבודה makes it invalid. A קל וחומר from a בעל מום is pushed back, and so is a proof from a זר. Together they form a הצד השוה: anyone forbidden to serve ruins the עבודה if he serves. The גמרא then asks where an אונן is forbidden to serve, and finds the ban in 'הן הקריבו'. The הצד השוה is attacked, because an אונן's ban has an exception for a כהן גדול. A טמא is added to answer that attack, and the three-way proof stands. רב משרשיא offers another proof by קל וחומר from a כהן who serves sitting. It survives the objection that a sitting person is unfit to testify. Next, רבא limits the משנה: an אונן disqualifies only a קרבן יחיד, and he learns this by קל וחומר from טומאה. רבא בר אהילאי shows three times that this kind of קל וחומר can be flipped to reach false results, and a סימן sums up his three arguments.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from a blemished כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes a קל וחומר: if a בעל מום, who may eat קדשים, ruins the עבודה, then an אונן, who may not eat, should surely ruin it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blemished כהן is allowed to eat sacrificial meat, and still, if he serves, he ruins the service. A mourner is not allowed to eat. Isn't it logical that if he serves, he ruins the service?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to find a source that an אונן who does the עבודה makes it invalid. It suggests a קל וחומר from a בעל מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating קדשים is treated as a sign of how close a כהן is to the קדשים. The בעל מום is the 'lighter' case because he may eat, yet he ruins the עבודה. The אונן is 'stricter' because he may not eat, so he should ruin the עבודה even more.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן with a physical blemish, who may not serve in the מקדש
A mourner on the day a close relative dies, before burial
He desecrated, meaning he made the עבודה invalid
He performed the עבודה (the sacrificial service)
Isn't it logical? The standard opening of a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. The בעל מום MAY eat קדשים but may not serve. The אונן may NOT eat. That difference is what powers the קל וחומר.

phrases.english: A blemished kohen, who does eat [sacrificial meat]:
if he served, he desecrated [the service];
a mourner, who does not eat [sacrificial meat]:
is it not logical that if he served, he desecrated?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the search for a source that an אונן ruins the עבודה
steps.raayaObject: That an אונן who serves desecrates the עבודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from בעל מום

steps.title: The blemished כהן has a special strictness
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is rejected. A בעל מום has an extra strictness: the Torah treats blemished animals the same as blemished כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a blemished כהן? He is special, because the Torah made the animals being offered like the כהנים offering them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the קל וחומר by finding something stricter about a בעל מום that an אונן does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish disqualifies both the animal and the כהן, so blemishes are a stronger kind of disqualification. Mourning has no such parallel, because there is no 'mourning animal'. So maybe only a blemish ruins the עבודה, and an אונן does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? The formula that points out what is special about the source case
In that, or since. It introduces the special feature
The animals offered are like the ones offering them, so a blemish disqualifies both

phrases.english: What about a blemished kohen?
For [the Torah] made, with him, those offered like those who offer!
phrases.notes: A blemish disqualifies an animal and also disqualifies a כהן, so here the animal and the כהן are treated alike.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from בעל מום alone
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A בעל מום has a stringency, קריבין כמקריבין, that an אונן lacks

steps.title: A non-כהן proves the point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a זר shows this strictness does not matter. A זר has no link to the animals, yet he still ruins the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-כהן will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case, a זר, to defend the conclusion against the objection in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No animal is disqualified for being 'non-priestly', so the קריבין כמקריבין idea does not apply to a זר. Still, a זר who serves ruins the עבודה. So that strictness cannot be the real reason a disqualified person ruins the עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן, who may never do the עבודה
Will prove. It brings a case that disproves the objection

phrases.english: A non-kohen will prove [it].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example showing the objection's feature is not needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a בעל מום ruins the עבודה, because of קריבין כמקריבין
steps.terutzMaskana: A זר ruins the עבודה without that feature, so the feature is not the reason

steps.title: A non-כהן can never be fixed
steps.stepSummary: The proof from זר is rejected. A זר is special because his problem can never be fixed, while an אונן will be fit to serve later.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a non-כהן? He is special, because he has no fix.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the זר proof by pointing out what is stricter about a זר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זר will never become a כהן, so his ban is permanent. An אונן's problem is temporary and ends once the mourning period passes. Maybe only a permanent ban ruins the עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: He has no fix. His disqualification can never be removed

phrases.english: What about a non-kohen?
For he has no remedy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the counter-proof of step 3
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A זר's disqualification is permanent, and an אונן's is not

steps.title: The blemished כהן answers back, and the argument circles
steps.stepSummary: The בעל מום answers the objection: his blemish can heal, yet while he is blemished he ruins the עבודה. Now the argument has gone full circle.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blemished כהן will prove it. And the argument has come back around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the first case, בעל מום, to answer the objection against זר. It notes that the argument has returned to where it started, which sets up the final move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish can heal, so a בעל מום does have a fix, and he still ruins the עבודה while blemished. So 'no fix' is not the reason. But the בעל מום was already weakened in step 2, so neither case can stand on its own. That is why the גמרא now turns to a different method.

keyTerms.meaning: And the argument has come back around. Each case answers the weakness of the other

phrases.english: A blemished kohen will prove [it].
And the argument has come back around.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection of step 4 and sets up the הצד השוה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example, followed by noting that the argument circles
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a permanent ban, like a זר's, ruins the עבודה
steps.terutzMaskana: A בעל מום has a fix and still ruins the עבודה, so permanence is not the reason

steps.title: The common feature proves that a mourner ruins the service
steps.stepSummary: Using a הצד השוה: בעל מום and זר each have a unique feature, but both are forbidden to serve and ruin the עבודה if they do. An אונן is also forbidden, so he ruins it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they share is that they are warned not to serve, and if they serve, they ruin the service. So I will also include a mourner. He is warned not to serve, so if he serves, he ruins the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches its conclusion by building a הצד השוה from the two cases. It concludes that an אונן who serves desecrates the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each special feature (קריבין כמקריבין for the בעל מום, 'no fix' for the זר) appears in only one case, so neither feature can be the cause. The only thing both cases share is being forbidden to serve. An אונן shares that feature, so he gets the same result.

keyTerms.meaning: The feature of this case is not like the feature of that case
The common feature. A proof built from what two cases share
They are warned, meaning they are forbidden to serve
I will also bring in. It applies the rule to the new case

steps.whatToRemember: A קל וחומר from בעל מום alone fails, and so does a proof from זר alone. Together they form a הצד השוה: anyone forbidden to serve who serves ruins the עבודה. That includes an אונן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the classic pattern: a קל וחומר is rejected, a יוכיח is brought, and the argument circles until a הצד השוה settles it. The result is that the עבודה of an אונן is invalid.

phrases.english: The aspect of this is not like the aspect of that,
and the aspect of that is not like the aspect of this;
the common element between them:
that they are warned [not to serve], and if they served, they desecrated;
so I too will bring in a mourner, who is warned [not to serve],
and if he served, he desecrated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the circular argument with a הצד השוה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An אונן is forbidden to serve, and if he serves he desecrates the עבודה, learned from the common feature of בעל מום and זר

steps.title: Where is an אונן warned not to serve?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that forbids an אונן to do the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is he (the אונן) warned not to serve?
steps.whatsHappening: The הצד השוה ended by saying 'an אונן is also forbidden to serve.' Now the גמרא stops to ask where the Torah says that. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הצד השוה only works if we already know an אונן is forbidden to serve. It uses that ban to prove he also ruins the עבודה. So the גמרא must find the ban written somewhere in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: warned / forbidden by a Torah warning
a mourner on the day a close relative died, before burial

phrases.english: Where is he warned?
phrases.notes: He means the אונן. The last step said he is forbidden to serve, so where does the Torah say so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the starting assumption of the הצד השוה in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that forbids an אונן to do the עבודה.

steps.title: Not from 'he shall not leave the מקדש'
steps.stepSummary: The first suggested source is rejected, because that פסוק already says 'he will not profane' outright.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the source is 'And from the מקדש he shall not go out', that פסוק already writes 'profaning' itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one פסוק as the source and turns it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'ומן המקדש לא יצא' goes on to say 'ולא יחלל', meaning 'he will not profane'. If that were the source, the Torah would already be saying openly that an אונן ruins the עבודה. Then the whole הצד השוה would be unnecessary. So the תנא of this derivation cannot be using this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say
profaning; here, ruining the עבודה
in itself, explicitly

phrases.english: If you say from "And from the Sanctuary he shall not go out,"
profaning itself is written in it!
phrases.notes: The same פסוק continues 'ולא יחלל', so there would be nothing left to prove.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to step 7 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only this proposed source, not the ban itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: This פסוק states חילול openly, which would make the הצד השוה pointless.

steps.title: The source is 'הן הקריבו'
steps.stepSummary: The ban comes from אהרן's words to משה, 'הן הקריבו', and this תנא holds that the חטאת was burned because of אנינות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes from 'Behold, they offered', and he holds that the חטאת was burned because of אנינות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real source of the ban on an אונן serving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the day נדב and אביהו died, a חטאת was burned instead of being eaten, and אהרן explained 'הן הקריבו'. This תנא understands the reason was that אהרן and his sons were אוננים. That shows an אונן is forbidden in the עבודה. But the פסוק does not say he ruins it, so the הצד השוה is still needed for that.

keyTerms.meaning: and he (this תנא) holds
the state of being an אונן
it (the חטאת) was burned

phrases.english: Rather, from "Behold, they offered"
and he holds it was burned because of acute mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after step 8 rejected the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban comes from 'הן הקריבו', read as showing the חטאת was burned because of אנינות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why a logical derivation was needed: this source gives a ban but does not say the עבודה is ruined.

steps.title: Attack on the הצד השוה: no exceptions
steps.stepSummary: בעל מום and זר share a strictness the אונן lacks: their ban never has an exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: One can refute it: what about their common point? Their ban never has an exception!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the conclusion of step 6 by finding a feature that בעל מום and זר share but an אונן does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הצד השוה breaks down if both sources share a stricter feature. A בעל מום or זר is never allowed to serve. An אונן is, though, since a כהן גדול may serve while an אונן. So perhaps only cases with no exception ruin the עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: one can refute (it)
its general rule was never permitted in any case

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying an אונן may serve in general. Only the כהן גדול has this exception. The point is that the אונן ban has some exception at all, while the other two have none.

phrases.english: It can be refuted:
What about the common element between them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means בעל מום and זר from step 6.

phrases.english: in that it was never permitted from its general rule!
phrases.notes: An אונן does have an exception: a כהן גדול may serve as an אונן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִפְרַךְ: מָה לְהַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the הצד השוה of step 6 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The הצד השוה from בעל מום and זר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources share a strictness (no exception to their ban) that the אונן lacks, so the derivation cannot reach the אונן.

steps.title: A טמא proves it
steps.stepSummary: A טמא כהן has an exception to his ban, yet he still ruins the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טמא will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the attack by pointing to a טמא כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on a טמא serving has an exception: טומאה is allowed for community קרבנות. Even so, a טמא who serves when he is not allowed ruins the עבודה. So having an exception does not stop a ban from ruining the עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: a ritually impure כהן
will prove

phrases.english: An impure one will prove it.
phrases.notes: A טמא may serve in community קרבנות, so his ban also has an exception, yet he still ruins the עבודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attack of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counterexample: a case with an exception that still ruins the עבודה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a ban with no exception ruins the עבודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A טמא shows an exception does not matter.

steps.title: But a טמא spreads טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The proof from טמא is rejected: a טמא is special because he makes others טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a טמא? He makes things impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from טמא by finding a stricter feature only he has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא passes his טומאה on to people and things. Maybe that is why he ruins the עבודה. An אונן does not pass his state on to anyone, so the טמא case cannot prove anything about him.

keyTerms.meaning: makes others impure

phrases.english: What about an impure one? He makes things impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 11.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A טמא has a unique strictness: he passes on טומאה.

steps.title: בעל מום and זר prove it
steps.stepSummary: בעל מום and זר do not spread anything, yet they ruin the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those (בעל מום and זר) will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the push-back by going back to בעל מום and זר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל מום and a זר do not pass their state on to anyone, yet they ruin the עבודה. So spreading טומאה is not the reason a טמא ruins it. Each case now covers the other's weak point.

keyTerms.meaning: those (the earlier cases)
will prove (plural)

phrases.english: Those will prove it.
phrases.notes: 'Those' means בעל מום and זר. Neither one makes anyone else into a בעל מום or a זר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counterexample: cases that do not spread their state yet still ruin the עבודה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טמא ruins the עבודה only because he spreads טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: בעל מום and זר show spreading is not the reason.

steps.title: The three-way הצד השוה stands
steps.stepSummary: The argument goes full circle. The shared feature of טמא, בעל מום and זר is that they are forbidden to serve, so an אונן, who is also forbidden, ruins the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument has gone back around, and so on. Their common point is that they are forbidden, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the derivation. All three cases together prove that an אונן ruins the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has its own special feature, but the others make up for it. What all three share is only that they are forbidden to serve, and each one ruins the עבודה. An אונן is forbidden too (from 'הן הקריבו'), so he also ruins it. The 'כו׳' tells us to fill in the same wording as the earlier הצד השוה.

keyTerms.meaning: the argument has come back around
etc.; finish the familiar wording
they are warned / forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: An אונן ruins the עבודה. This is learned from a הצד השוה of טמא, בעל מום and זר: all are forbidden to serve, and all ruin the עבודה. The ban on an אונן itself comes from 'הן הקריבו'.

phrases.english: And the argument returns, etc.,
Their common element is that they are warned, etc.
phrases.notes: Fill in: and they ruin the עבודה, so an אונן, who is also forbidden, ruins it too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the cycle of steps 10-13 into a final derivation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An אונן ruins the עבודה, learned from the shared feature of טמא, בעל מום and זר.

steps.title: Their bans are never lifted for a High Priest
steps.stepSummary: The הצד השוה of טמא, בעל מום and זר can be refuted: none of their bans is ever lifted for a כהן גדול bringing a private קרבן, but an אונן כהן גדול may serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us refute this: what about the shared feature of these cases? None of their bans is ever lifted, not even for a כהן גדול bringing a private offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the conclusion of step 14 with a new difference between the three cases and an אונן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אונן who is a כהן גדול is allowed to serve, even with a private offering. The three cases (טמא, בעל מום, זר) never get that permission for a כהן גדול with a private offering. So maybe their bans are stricter, and that is why they ruin the עבודה, while an אונן's lighter ban does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Let one refute; let us find a weakness in the proof
The common feature shared by several cases, used as a proof
The High Priest
An offering brought by one person, not by the whole community

phrases.english: But let one refute:
What about the common feature among them?
For they were not permitted out of their general ban
for a High Priest with an individual's offering!
phrases.notes: The contrast he has in mind: a כהן גדול who is an אונן may serve, even with a private offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הצד השוה conclusion reached in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The הצד השוה derivation from טמא, בעל מום and זר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three cases share a strictness the אונן lacks: no permission for a כהן גדול with a private offering. So their shared feature may not carry over to an אונן.

steps.title: The category of impurity is permitted in some cases
steps.stepSummary: The challenge fails, because the category of טומאה is permitted in some cases, so 'never permitted' is not true of all three.
steps.simpleTranslation: The category of טומאה, at least, was permitted in some cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 15 and saves the הצד השוה proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge needed all three cases to share a ban that is never lifted. But טומאה as a category is permitted in some situations, for example for communal offerings. So טמא does not have that strictness, and the challenge falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The category (name) of impurity, as a general idea
At least
Was permitted

phrases.english: The category of impurity, at least,
was permitted.
phrases.notes: He means that טומאה is allowed in some cases, like communal offerings, even if not for a כהן גדול's private offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies that the strictness is shared by all three cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three bans are never lifted, so they are stricter than an אונן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The category of טומאה is lifted in some cases, so the strictness is not shared, and the הצד השוה proof stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The הצד השוה proof survives: טמא, בעל מום and זר ruin the עבודה because they are forbidden to serve, and an אונן is also forbidden.

steps.title: A new proof from a priest who serves sitting down
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא learns the אונן by קל וחומר from a יושב: a sitting כהן may eat קדשים yet ruins the עבודה, so an אונן who may not eat surely ruins it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: We learn it by קל וחומר from a כהן who serves sitting down. A sitting כהן is allowed to eat קדשים, and still, if he serves, he ruins the עבודה. An אונן is not even allowed to eat. Isn't it logical that if he serves, he ruins it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא offers a brand-new way to prove that an אונן ruins the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן must stand while serving, so one who serves sitting ruins the עבודה, even though he is fully allowed to eat קדשים. An אונן is weaker, because he may not eat קדשים at all. So if the stronger one (יושב) ruins the עבודה, the weaker one (אונן) should surely ruin it too.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
A כהן who does the service while sitting
Ruined (literally desecrated) the service
A mourner on the day a close relative died

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said:
It is derived by a kal vachomer from a sitting [priest];
phrases.notes: A כהן has to stand while serving, so one who serves sitting down is not doing it properly.

phrases.english: just as a sitting one, who may eat [sacrificial meat],
if he served, he ruined [the service];
an onen, who may not eat,
is it not logical that if he served, he ruined it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא אָמַר: אָתְיָא בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מִיּוֹשֵׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same law that the הצד השוה proved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אונן ruins the עבודה, learned by קל וחומר from a כהן who serves sitting.

steps.title: A sitting person is unfit to testify
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is challenged: a sitting person has an extra weakness, since he is unfit for testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a sitting person? He has a special weakness: he is unfit to give testimony!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in רב משרשיא's קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the 'lighter' case is lighter in every way. But sitting has another weakness: witnesses must stand, so a sitting person cannot testify. Maybe that weakness is why sitting ruins the עבודה, and an אונן does not have it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about...?': the opening of a refutation pointing to a difference
Unfit to be a witness

phrases.english: What about a sitting one?
For he is unfit for testimony!
phrases.notes: Witnesses have to stand when they testify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב משרשיא's קל וחומר from יושב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sitting carries a strictness (unfit for testimony) that the אונן lacks, so the יושב is not truly the lighter case.

steps.title: Learn from a sitting Torah scholar
steps.stepSummary: Learn from a sitting תלמיד חכם, who may testify sitting, yet still ruins the עבודה if he serves sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn it from a תלמיד חכם who sits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by choosing a sitting person who does not have the testimony problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית דין may let a תלמיד חכם sit while testifying, so for him sitting does not cause unfitness for testimony. Yet if he serves sitting, he still ruins the עבודה. So the testimony issue is not the reason, and the קל וחומר works again.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar

phrases.english: From a sitting Torah scholar.
phrases.notes: A Torah scholar may be allowed to sit while testifying, so the testimony problem does not apply to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks a narrower example that lacks the extra weakness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sitting ruins the עבודה because a sitting person is unfit to testify.
steps.terutzMaskana: A sitting תלמיד חכם may testify, yet still ruins the עבודה, so the קל וחומר holds.

steps.title: The category of sitting is still unfit for testimony
steps.stepSummary: Even with the תלמיד חכם, the general category of sitting is still unfit for testimony, so the challenge returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about sitting as a category? In general, sitting makes a person unfit to testify!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תלמיד חכם is only an exception. Sitting, as a general category, still makes a person unfit to testify. So the argument claims the whole category of יושב carries an extra weakness the אונן lacks.

keyTerms.meaning: The category (name) of 'sitting', as a general idea

phrases.english: What about the category of sitting?
For it is unfit for testimony!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְשֵׁם יוֹשֵׁב, שֶׁכֵּן פָּסוּל לְעֵדוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 19, the same way step 16 used 'שם טומאה'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer from a sitting תלמיד חכם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The individual exception does not remove the weakness of the general category of sitting.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the reversal. In step 16 the גמרא itself used a category (שם טומאה) to answer. Here the challenger uses a category (שם יוֹשֵׁב) to attack, and in the next step the גמרא will say a category cannot attack.

steps.title: A category cannot refute a proof
steps.stepSummary: The general category of sitting cannot be used to refute a proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The category of sitting does not refute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 20 by rejecting this kind of refutation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A refutation must point to a real weakness in the actual case we learn from. The sitting תלמיד חכם himself is fit to testify. A weakness in the general category that does not apply to him cannot break the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not refute; cannot be used to break a proof

phrases.english: The category of sitting does not refute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the method of the refutation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A weakness of the general category can refute the proof.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a weakness of the actual case can refute; a category cannot.

steps.title: Even so, combine sitting with one of the other cases
steps.stepSummary: Even if a category can refute, the אונן is learned from יושב together with one of the other cases (טמא, בעל מום or זר) through their shared feature.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if you say the category can refute, we learn it from יושב together with one of those other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a backup answer, so the law is proven either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case alone has its own weakness: sitting is unfit for testimony, and the others have weaknesses of their own. But put יושב together with טמא, בעל מום or זר, and the weakness of one is not found in the other. What they share is that the כהן is not fit to serve and still ruins the עבודה, and that is true of an אונן too.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; introduces a backup answer
It comes; it is derived
One of those (earlier cases)

phrases.english: And if you say it does refute,
it is derived from a sitting one and from one of those.
phrases.notes: 'Those' means the cases from before: a טמא, a בעל מום, or a זר.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר פָּרֵיךְ – אָתְיָא מִיּוֹשֵׁב וּמֵחֲדָא מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second answer to the קשיא of step 20, joining רב משרשיא's case with the earlier הצד השוה cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Builds a new הצד השוה that cancels each case's special weakness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The testimony weakness of sitting breaks the proof.
steps.terutzMaskana: Combining יושב with one of the other cases leaves only the shared feature, so an אונן ruins the עבודה.
steps.whatToRemember: Either way, an אונן who serves ruins the עבודה: by רב משרשיא's קל וחומר, or by a הצד השוה from יושב plus one of טמא, בעל מום or זר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא protects a הצד השוה: when each case has its own weakness, pairing them cancels those weaknesses and leaves only the shared point.

steps.title: רבא: The mourner disqualifies only an individual's offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that an אונן is פסול. רבא says this applies only to a קרבן יחיד, and that with a קרבן צבור the אונן's service is valid. He bases this on a קל וחומר from טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says an acute mourner is disqualified. רבא said: that is only for a private person's offering. For a public offering, his service counts, and we learn this by קל וחומר from ritual impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה's line about an אונן. רבא then limits that rule to private offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just says an אונן is פסול, with no details. רבא adds that the rule only covers a קרבן יחיד. For a קרבן צבור, an אונן's service is מרצה. He announces that his source is a קל וחומר from טומאה, which he spells out in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An acute mourner: someone whose close relative died that same day
An offering brought by a private person
An offering brought for the whole community
It counts: the offering is accepted and does its job
They only taught this about...: a phrase that narrows the earlier rule

phrases.english: An acute mourner is disqualified.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד,
phrases.english: Rava said: They taught this only about an individual's offering,
but with a communal offering, it effects acceptance,
by a fortiori reasoning from ritual impurity;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. Steps 17-22 were about a יושב and how we learn the rule for an אונן; now the גמרא asks how far the אונן's disqualification reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אונן disqualifies only a קרבן יחיד. His service on a קרבן צבור is valid.

steps.title: רבא spells out the comparison to impurity
steps.stepSummary: טומאה is never allowed for a כהן גדול on a private offering, yet it is allowed for an ordinary כהן on a public offering. אנינות is allowed for a כהן גדול on a private offering, so it should surely be allowed for an ordinary כהן on a public offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Impurity was never permitted for a כהן גדול with a private offering, yet it was permitted for an ordinary כהן with a public offering. Mourning was permitted for a כהן גדול with a private offering. So surely it is permitted for an ordinary כהן with a public offering!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא lays out the full קל וחומר that proves his rule from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאה looks like the stricter prohibition, because even a כהן גדול may never serve with it on a private offering. Even so, it is set aside for a קרבן צבור. אנינות looks more lenient, since a כהן גדול may serve as an אונן. So רבא argues it should certainly be set aside for a קרבן צבור.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity
The status of being an אונן, an acute mourner
An exception was made to its general prohibition
The High Priest
An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול
Isn't it only logical...?: the closing line of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: Just as impurity, whose general prohibition was not relaxed
for a High Priest with an individual's offering –
was permitted for an ordinary priest with a communal offering;
then acute mourning, whose general prohibition was relaxed
for a High Priest with an individual's offering –
is it not logical that it is permitted
for an ordinary priest with a communal offering?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the קל וחומר that רבא announced in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that an אונן's service on a קרבן צבור is valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from טומאה, which is set aside for a קרבן צבור even though it is never allowed for a כהן גדול on a קרבן יחיד.

steps.title: רבא בר אהילאי flips the reasoning against the mourning כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר אהילאי shows that the same kind of קל וחומר can be built the other way. It would then forbid a כהן גדול to serve as an אונן on a private offering, which is clearly wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר אהילאי objected: By the same reasoning, mourning should not be allowed for a כהן גדול with a private offering. Impurity is allowed for an ordinary כהן with a public offering, yet it is not allowed for a כהן גדול with a private offering. Mourning is not allowed for an ordinary כהן with a public offering, so surely it should not be allowed for a כהן גדול with a private offering!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר אהילאי attacks רבא's proof. He builds a reverse קל וחומר from the same two facts and reaches a result that is known to be false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time he starts from the leniency of טומאה for an ordinary כהן on a קרבן צבור. He uses it to make טומאה look like the 'lighter' prohibition, and then concludes that a כהן גדול אונן should be forbidden. But a כהן גדול is in fact allowed to serve as an אונן. So this way of comparing the two prohibitions leads to a wrong answer, and that throws doubt on רבא's קל וחומר too.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it
The אמורא who raises the challenge
It should be permitted

steps.confusionAlert: רבא בר אהילאי is not really claiming that a כהן גדול אונן is forbidden. He builds a conclusion that he knows is wrong in order to show that this style of קל וחומר does not hold up.

phrases.english: Rava bar Ahilai objected to this:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תּוּתַּר אֲנִינוּת אֵצֶל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: Acute mourning should not be permitted for a High Priest
with an individual's offering, by a fortiori reasoning:
And just as impurity, which was permitted
for an ordinary priest with a communal offering –

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הוּתְּרָה אֵצֶל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד;
phrases.english: was not permitted for a High Priest with an individual's offering;
then acute mourning, which was not permitted
for an ordinary priest with a communal offering –
is it not logical that it should not be permitted
for a High Priest with an individual's offering?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קל וחומר of step 24 by building a reverse קל וחומר from the same facts.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's קל וחומר from טומאה to אנינות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Built the same way, a קל וחומר leads to a conclusion we know is false: that a כהן גדול אונן may not serve on a private offering. So this method of comparing the two prohibitions is unreliable.

steps.title: The reverse reasoning would also permit an impure High Priest
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר אהילאי continues: the same method could also prove that a כהן גדול may serve while טמא on a private offering, learning from the leniency for an אונן. This is also clearly wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: And impurity should be allowed for a כהן גדול with a private offering, by קל וחומר. Mourning is not allowed for an ordinary כהן with a public offering, yet it is allowed for a כהן גדול with a private offering. Impurity is allowed for an ordinary כהן with a public offering, so surely it should be allowed for a כהן גדול with a private offering!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר אהילאי adds a second false conclusion, this time about טומאה, to show again that this kind of reasoning breaks down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now he starts from the leniency of אנינות for a כהן גדול. He uses it to 'prove' that טומאה should also be allowed for a כהן גדול on a private offering. But טומאה is never allowed for a כהן גדול on a קרבן יחיד. Each prohibition has its own separate leniency, so neither can be used to prove the other, and that is what knocks down רבא's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: And it should be permitted
And just as...: the opening word of the first half of a קל וחומר
By an argument from the lighter case to the stricter case

steps.whatToRemember: טומאה and אנינות each have their own different leniency. טומאה is set aside for a קרבן צבור, and אנינות is set aside for a כהן גדול. A קל וחומר from one to the other can be pushed in either direction and gives wrong results, so רבא's proof is in doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key weakness of a קל וחומר. If each side has a leniency the other side lacks, the argument can be flipped, and then it proves nothing.

phrases.english: And impurity should be permitted for a High Priest
with an individual's offering, by a fortiori reasoning:
And just as acute mourning, which was not permitted
for an ordinary priest with a communal offering –

phrases.aramaic: הוּתְּרָה אֵצֶל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד;
phrases.english: was permitted for a High Priest with an individual's offering;
then impurity, which was permitted
for an ordinary priest with a communal offering –
is it not logical that it is permitted
for a High Priest with an individual's offering?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּתַּר טוּמְאָה אֵצֶל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second part of רבא בר אהילאי's objection: a further reverse קל וחומר, this time reaching a false result about טומאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's קל וחומר from טומאה to אנינות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Using the כהן גדול's leniency for אנינות, the same method would wrongly allow a טמא כהן גדול to serve on a קרבן יחיד. So comparing these two separate leniencies is not valid.

steps.title: The method would also forbid impurity on a communal offering
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר אהילאי adds a third flipped קל וחומר. Since אנינות is allowed for a כהן גדול on a קרבן יחיד but forbidden for a כהן הדיוט on a קרבן צבור, then טומאה, which is stricter, should surely be forbidden for a כהן הדיוט on a קרבן צבור. That result is wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: And impurity should not be allowed for an ordinary כהן on a communal offering, by a קל וחומר: אנינות is allowed for a כהן גדול on a private offering, and still it is not allowed for an ordinary כהן on a communal offering. טומאה is not allowed for a כהן גדול on a private offering. Surely, then, it should not be allowed for an ordinary כהן on a communal offering!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר אהילאי gives a third example of how רבא's kind of קל וחומר can be built in reverse. This time it would forbid a טמא כהן from serving on a קרבן צבור, which we know is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This argument starts from the plain rule of the משנה, without רבא's leniency: an ordinary כהן who is an אונן may not serve, even on a public offering. It then moves to טומאה, which is stricter because even a כהן גדול may not serve while טמא. The conclusion contradicts a known הלכה, since טומאה is allowed for a קרבן צבור, so this method of reasoning cannot be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול
A communal offering, brought for the whole people
A private offering, brought by one person
The state of a mourner on the day a close relative dies
Is it not logical? (the closing line of a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא בר אהילאי holds that טומאה is forbidden on a קרבן צבור. He is showing that the reasoning leads to a result everyone knows is false, so the reasoning itself is weak.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the third of three flipped arguments. Together they show that a קל וחומר which can be turned around this easily is not a reliable source.

phrases.english: And impurity should not be permitted
for an ordinary priest on a communal offering,
by an a fortiori argument:
And just as acute mourning,
which was permitted for a High Priest
on an individual's offering,
was not permitted for an ordinary priest
phrases.notes: This follows the plain rule of the משנה, that an אונן may not serve, without רבא's leniency.

phrases.english: on a communal offering;
then impurity, which was not permitted
for a High Priest on an individual's offering,
is it not logical that it should not be permitted
for an ordinary priest on a communal offering?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא תּוּתַּר טוּמְאָה אֵצֶל כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט בְּקׇרְבַּן צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and last in the series of flipped קל וחומר arguments by רבא בר אהילאי, after steps 25 and 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's קל וחומר (step 24) that allows an אונן to serve on a קרבן צבור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same structure, starting from the stringency of אנינות for a כהן הדיוט, would forbid טומאה on a קרבן צבור. That contradicts the known rule that טומאה is allowed for public offerings, so the method is unreliable.

steps.title: A memory aid for the three rejections
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a short list of key words, a סימן, to help the learner remember the three flipped arguments of רבא בר אהילאי in order.
steps.simpleTranslation: And should not be permitted, and should not be permitted, mourning, and impurity, impurity, individual, and individual, communal: this is a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to give a memory aid. It is not a new argument. It is a string of key words that recalls the three rejections we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words point to the main ideas of each flipped argument: two arguments that end with "should not be permitted," and the topics they move between (אנינות, טומאה, private and communal offerings). Back when learning was memorized by heart, such word lists kept the order of arguments straight.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, a list of key words to help remember a series of statements

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's קל וחומר from טומאה to allow an אונן on a קרבן צבור was attacked three times by רבא בר אהילאי. Each time, the same kind of reasoning built in reverse led to a result that is clearly wrong.

phrases.english: (And should not be permitted, and should not be permitted,
phrases.notes: Here the round brackets just hold a memory aid. They are not a correction of the text.

phrases.english: acute mourning, and impurity, impurity,
individual, and individual, communal: a mnemonic)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the series of three rejections with a memory aid listing their key words.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The three flipped arguments of רבא בר אהילאי are summed up in a סימן. The series shows that רבא's style of קל וחומר can be reversed and is therefore questionable.
